ab_ac_phale.blurb: Acéphale is a sport-only limestone crag on the forested flanks of Heart Mountain near Canmore, in Alberta's Bow Valley. The rock is hard, blocky, blue-streaked limestone that is rough on the skin, and routes run roughly 15 to 35 metres. The grades are hard, mostly 5.12 and 5.13, with fewer at 5.11 and 5.14 and only a few at 5.10. The walls get no direct sun and can be chilly, and the shade keeps climbing going into hotter months. The approach is steep, around 30 to 45 minutes. Upper Wall holds the most climbs, with harder, shorter and more intense routes, while Lower Wall offers power-endurance lines and more variety in rock and style. Down Under is a smaller sector.

ca_west_face_the.blurb: The West Face is a bouldering area near Doyle in northeast California, spread through rugged canyons with hundreds of acres of boulder-studded ground. The rock is gritty monzonite. Problems range from one-move sit starts and topouts to highballs with no-fall landings, and most fall between V0 and V4, with a handful at V5 and V6. Pinkland holds the most climbs: a jumbled field of boulders over roughly 1,000 acres, split by a ravine into Pinkland proper and the Highlands, and easy to get lost in. Cow Skull Boulders and Homestead Canyon follow.

co_forest_boulders.blurb: Forest Boulders is a bouldering area in the Wonderland part of Colorado's South Platte, at about 8,200 feet, among the trees around Puff's Lair and Walls of Honah Lee. Two kinds of granite show up: classic coarse South Platte granite that is featureless and hard on the skin, and a solid, fine-grained granite. Nearly everything is bouldering, with most problems between V0 and V6 and a few at V10 and V11. The many small boulders include Morph Dusseldorf, Lost Boys Boulder, The Lionfish and Doctor's Office. The roped climbing at neighbouring Castle View Crags is on a mix of granite, gneiss and pegmatite.

co_north_rim_routes.blurb: North Rim Routes are the long trad climbs on the north side of Colorado's Black Canyon of the Gunnison, south of Crawford. The canyon is very deep and narrow, and its climbing is full-on adventure: multi-pitch traditional routes in remote terrain, with route-finding and runouts, and loose rock is a concern across the canyon. The north side is described as warmer and brighter than the walls across the canyon. Grades are mostly 5.10 to 5.12, with a few easier lines. North Chasm View Wall holds the most climbs, followed by Aretes and SOB Gully (skier's left side), with The Painted Wall and The Checkerboard Wall also here. Across the park, peak climbing runs from mid-April to early June and from mid-September to early November.

ks_the_lost_city_of_critzer.blurb: The Lost City of Critzer is a small cluster of limestone bouldering in Kansas, near Critzer Lake. Shroomie’s Boulder Field holds the most climbs, on a ridge of limestone mushroom formations roughly 8 to 12 feet tall, with problems that use finger, hand and fist jams and off-width cracks as well as horizontal and vertical movement. Placer Ridge is a limestone ridge 8 to 15 feet tall on the west side of where the headwaters meet Critzer Lake, and its rock is described as exceptional for Kansas. Everything here is bouldering, with most problems between V0 and V4 and a few reaching V7.

mt_yankee_jim.blurb: Yankee Jim is a bouldering area in Paradise Valley, Montana, about an hour from Bozeman and at roughly 5,000 feet. The boulders are a sparse cluster of quality gneiss blocks with interesting features and bands. Nearly everything is bouldering, from V0 up to V11, with most problems between V0 and V4. Spring and fall are described as best, though chasing sun and shade makes year-round climbing possible, and cold days give better friction. Locomotive Boulders holds the most climbs, followed by Campground Boulders and Mile 13 Boulders. Within Locomotive Boulders, Anderson Cave is a shady, flat sector with climbing on the undercut of a cliff.
